title: Sweden's Election-Year Economy: Growth Data and a Food Tax Cut Fuel a Battle… · 07 Sep
keywords: Sweden economy, Swedish GDP, food VAT cut, cost of living, Swedish inflation, CPI, HICP, Swedish election, Ulf Kristersson, economic recovery, EU inflation, household finances, value-added tax, disinflation, Swedish politics
notes: Sweden's governing bloc is heading into election season armed with stronger-than-expected second-quarter growth figures and falling inflation, framing both as proof that its tax-cutting agenda is working. But the opposition argues that one quarter of positive data obscures persistent pressures on wages, housing, and public services. At the centre of the dispute is a temporary cut to food value-added tax, which ministers say is already relieving household costs — a claim the numbers support only in part.
